<description>
Follow-up to #36011

When a connection handle outlives its signal, a callback that was still connected at signal destruction stays alive, and the handle continues to report `connected() == true`. The referenced PR fix made an explicit `disconnect()` call release the callback. However, destroying the signal still did not disconnect its callbacks automatically, as pointed out by the author in this [#36011 comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36011#discussion_r4459623066).

This PR's commit disconnects each callback when its signal is destroyed. It extends the `callback_destruction` test to verify that destroying the signal also releases an idle callback’s captured state and the surviving handle gets disconnected, as suggested in this [#36011 comment](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36011#discussion_r4459623272).
</description>

[2026-11-20] rc:4645913711 inline on src/util/btcsignals.h by psychemist:
I considered removing each `holder` from the vector before disconnecting it:

```suggestion
        while (!m_connections.empty()) {
            auto holder{std::move(m_connections.back())};
            m_connections.pop_back();
```

Codex suggested that if one of the callback's captures calls `connect()` on the same signal from its destructor, it can modify `m_connections` in-place, invalidating the for loop’s iterator. I haven’t seen an example of this happening in Bitcoin Core so I kept the loop.
